papers.title: Two-timescale variational Q-learning for ergodic risk-sensitive control of Markov chains
papers.abstract: We propose a variational Q-learning algorithm for the ergodic risk-sensitive control of a discrete-time Markov chain with finite state and action spaces and an unknown transition kernel. The proposed algorithm is a two-timescale stochastic approximation algorithm, where the slow iteration solves for the fixed point of the multiplicative Bellman equation cast in a variational form, while the fast iteration solves the associated optimization problem over the probability simplex that stems from the variational representation. We prove that the iterates converge almost surely to the risk-sensitive Q-function and maximizing transition kernel. The proof adapts the ODE method for two-timescale stochastic approximation, where we analyze the global asymptotic stability of the equilibria of the corresponding fast and slow ODEs as well as bound the trajectory of the fast ODE away from zero. The main challenge lies in proving that, almost surely, the slow iterates are norm-bounded and the fast iterates are bounded below away from zero on the support of the transition kernel. We address this by using a fluid scaling approach for the slow iteration combined with tailored estimates for the fast iteration to control a certain fluid-scaled relative entropy error that arises in the ODE approximation. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithm and compare it with the existing risk-sensitive Q-learning algorithms.

papers.title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
papers.abstract: Can we distinguish fully AI-generated reviews from those using AI only to rewrite human judgement? Furthermore, can we do so reliably when reviews are generated from diverse AI models and workflows across scientific domains? To this end, we introduce PeerReveal, a new detector that grounds its decisions in learned relationships between a review's claims and reference claims drawn from AI-generated reviews of the same paper, complemented by review-level textual signals. We evaluate PeerReveal on PeerShift, a new, challenging test set of 5,430 reviews spanning multiple domains, including machine learning, life sciences, and social sciences, combining variation in disciplinary review conventions with diverse AI review-production mechanisms. With regular training, PeerReveal achieves 70.52% pooled Macro-F1 on this benchmark, improving over the strongest baseline by 11.48 points. We develop an effective and practical adversarial training framework that further improves the detector's generalization using a small local generator optimized to produce challenging reviews, raising pooled Macro-F1 from 70.52% to 82.40%. These results show that robust AI-review detection benefits from richer review-level evidence and adversarial training on more challenging generation processes.

papers.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_θ$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<θ<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.

papers.title: DiffER$^2$: Diffusion Ensembles for Retrosynthesis Prediction with SMILES Adapted Particle Guidance
papers.abstract: Computational retrosynthesis prediction has the potential to reduce development time for newly discovered drugs by automatically generating potential reactions for a target product. Data-driven approaches commonly treat this as a sequence-to-sequence generation task on SMILES strings. In this work, we construct ensembles of discrete-time and continuous-time diffusion models for molecular generation and incorporate guidance mechanisms for improved output diversity. We propose an adaptation of particle guidance to SMILES sequence generation which significantly improves the number of unique molecules generated by diffusion ensembles while increasing top-k accuracy. These results further expand the efficacy of discrete diffusion for SMILES generation, and our empirical analyses offer new insights into the capabilities of diffusion models for chemical retrosynthesis.

papers.title: Deleted square of a cone over a graph
papers.abstract: The deleted square of a topological space is a subspace of the Cartesian product of this space with itself, obtained by removing the diagonal. Conjecturally, the deleted square of a cone over a graph has the homotopy type of a wedge sum of spheres of dimensions at most 3. We propose a geometric construction that is a key motivation for the conjecture and provides a major step towards its proof, while yielding direct results on deleted squares of certain families of graphs.

papers.title: Robust Certification of Non-projective Qubit Measurements without Inputs
papers.abstract: Positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) beyond projective simulation (aka non-projective measurements) offer advantages over projective measurements, motivating their certification directly from observed statistics. Here, we show that this certification can be achieved robustly without input randomness, using only the joint outcome distribution of two measurement devices. We consider two spatially separated observers whose only shared resource is an uncharacterised two-qubit state. Each observer performs a local measurement. In the projective-simulable case, the measurement device privately randomises over qubit projective measurements and applies arbitrary classical post-processing to their outcomes. In the noiseless regime, we identify three- and four-outcome anti-correlations that certify that both local measurements lie beyond projective simulation. To establish noise robustness, we develop a non-linear covariance witness that combines the geometry of projective measurements with a contraction bound valid for every two-qubit state. For the correlations generated by identical qubit trine measurements or identical qubit SIC-POVM on noisy qubit singlet, we obtain exact critical white-noise fractions of (1/4) and (1/3), respectively. Below these thresholds, no pair of projective-simulable measurements on any two-qubit state can reproduce these correlations. We present explicit projective simulations that attain the thresholds and cover the remaining noise range. Finally, the same method yields a strictly positive noise tolerance for certification whenever both observers apply the same extremal qubit POVM with three or four non-zero effects to a depolarised qubit singlet. These results establish a general analytic framework for certifying non-projective qubit measurement resources without input randomness.

papers.title: Skeptic: Grounding Failure Diagnosis for Robot Skill Discovery
papers.abstract: Robot agents discover reusable skills by revising programs from execution feedback and retaining experience for later tasks. This process can fail when an agent treats an unsuccessful program as evidence that the task is physically impossible, ending exploration with revision budget remaining. We study this failure in Qwen3.8-27B and examine two decisions that shape skill discovery: I) how execution failures are diagnosed, and II) which lessons enter the shared skill library. Failure diagnosis requires the agent to reconstruct physical action effects from multimodal traces, while independent reproduction of a proposed repair does not require adequate task performance from its source program. We introduce Skeptic, a training-free protocol that uses measured action outcomes to guide repair and measured task success to govern skill admission. A grounded event log reports action effects and object end states from depth images and proprioception, separating sensor observations from inferred diagnoses. Verified promotion adds a development-success requirement on the source program to the existing independent reproduction check. Across 60 audited tasks, the mean number of tasks with false impossibility judgments decreases from 19.5 to 8.5 per campaign. On 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks and seven Robosuite tasks, Skeptic improves held-out success by 14.9 and 11.7 percentage points, with frozen model weights and the same program-revision budget.

papers.title: An iterative procedure for statistical calibration
papers.abstract: We study the iterative proportional fitting procedure (IPFP) under multiple pushforward constraints, motivated by model calibration. The goal is to find a distribution on model parameters whose pushforward by models matches data distributions. The classic convergence result of IPFP under marginal constraints establish convergence of IPFP under suitable regularity conditions and develop a variant of sequential importance sampling to approximate the iterative procedure. We also propose a related procedure for constructing a high probability parameter region. Simulation studies illustrate the performance of these methods. Finally, we apply IPFP to COVID19 ensemble forecasting. Variation of Covid strains across regions can lead to variation in surge rates and thus affect forecasting accuracy. To capture the variation, we estimate a probability distribution of epidemiological model parameters using early stage surge data from an ensemble of regions. We then propagate the distribution through the model to forecast both the ensemble's overall trend and its variability.

papers.title: Non-manipulability and Approachability Beyond Two-Player Games
papers.abstract: We study the problem of guaranteeing non-manipulability and low regret for $n-1$ independent learners in an $n$-player repeated general game with one optimizer. Non-manipulability is a property which guarantees that learning agents can prevent a strategic opponent from exploiting their learning dynamics for its own benefit, while no-regret provides guarantees to a learner with respect to a fixed static benchmark. This problem is well understood in games with a single learner and a single optimizer, where the intersection of non-manipulable and no-regret algorithms is exactly the class of all no-swap regret algorithms. But having multiple independent learners introduces a fundamental constraint: without shared randomness, the learners' joint mixed actions must remain product distributions and individual no-swap regret guarantees need not provide a guarantee of non-manipulability. Our core contributions are as follows. We introduce a set of $n-1$ algorithms that $n-1$ learners can play which individually guarantee sublinear swap regret and, when played in conjunction with each other, jointly guarantee non-manipulability against an optimizer. These algorithms require the computation of a Nash equilibrium at every timestep, and we show that this computational cost is inherent in general games. We construct a reduction from computing Nash in $(n-1)$-player games to finding $n-1$ jointly non-manipulable no-external regret algorithms. Therefore, polynomial time algorithms which guarantee multi-learner non-manipulability in conjunction with no-external regret do not exist unless PPAD $\subseteq$ FBPP. In order to construct these algorithms, we develop new techniques for Blackwell approachability beyond $2$-player games. We provide a general characterization for sets which are approachable by $n-1$ players without correlated randomness.

papers.title: FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
papers.abstract: Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation (ASHG) leveraging large language models (LLMs) aims to harness their strengths in knowledge integration, logical reasoning, and text generation for efficiently producing innovative, verifiable scientific hypotheses. However, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) insufficient fine-grained knowledge representation, as unstructured context impairs LLM comprehension and reasoning; (ii) lack of knowledge evolution traceability, constraining the generation of innovative cross-domain conjectures; (iii) absence of human-inspired and role-specialized multi-agent collaboration, failing to leverage the efficient innovation mechanisms arising from cognitive diversity and division of labor among expert roles to complete the full ASHG-evaluation loop. To address these limitations, we propose the Fine-grained Inspiration Graph-empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration framework (FIG-MAC) including: (i) Fine-grained Inspiration Graph module (FIG), to obtain fine-grained structured knowledge representations, where nodes represent academic semantic units and edges encode heuristic relationships among them; (ii) ontology-guided hybrid reasoning module, which follows the FIG ontology to construct structured reasoning paths and uses vector search to enrich them with semantic evidence, to obtain the traceable scientific conjecture paths; (iii) role-specialized Multi-Agent framework, inspired by real scientific teamwork, enabling a closed-loop process of scientific conjecture generation, screening, and validation. Experimental results demonstrate that FIG-MAC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on source diversity, provenance-adjusted novelty, and raw novelty.

papers.title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
papers.abstract: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

papers.title: EgoCARBS: Egocentric Video Meets Active Acoustics for Kitchen Action Understanding
papers.abstract: Egocentric video records what a person looks at, but often misses what their body does: the hands leave the frame, and arm motion goes unseen. An exocentric camera recovers this context, but it must be installed wherever the activity happens. Active acoustic sensing can recover it from the wearables themselves: a device's speaker emits inaudible chirps, and its microphone senses the motion of the hands, arms, and nearby objects from their echoes. Yet no public dataset pairs it with egocentric video. We present EgoCARBS, with two deliverables. The first is a multimodal dataset and benchmark: 15 participants cook unscripted meals in their own kitchens wearing camera glasses and an off-the-shelf smartwatch that both sense with active acoustics, synchronized with egocentric and exocentric video and the watch's audio and IMU, with 4,019 verb-noun action annotations in 11.4 hours. The second is a study of what the wearables add to egocentric video. On verb recognition, they add at least as much as an exocentric camera for participants seen in training, and even more for new participants, for whom the exocentric camera does not help. Active acoustics alone provides most of this gain, and helps most where the camera does not see the hands. Trimmed action recognition, detection, and anticipation remain open. We will release the data, our data collection and annotation tools, and pre-trained models.

papers.title: The Phases of Hierarchy
papers.abstract: We develop a dynamical phase theory of hierarchy, in which depth decides whether a population of size $N$ that revises its own environment can correct it without overcorrecting. The statistics that let a large majority detect a small bias - the basis of the Condorcet jury theorem - also make its response grow as $\sqrt{N}$. Fed back into the environment it is judging, this sharpening destabilises the matched state through a flip bifurcation at a critical loop gain, which we obtain analytically for a class of models we term adaptive normal forms. We show that this instability can be attenuated by hierarchical layering, requiring a depth scaling logarithmically with $N$. This recovers known logarithmic bounds in organisational economics directly from dynamic stability conditions. Hierarchical depth carries its own costs however, and by analysing the signal chain transmission up the hierarchy we show that beyond a finite depth no correction reaches the top before its deadline, and that below it the cost of arrival grows exponentially with depth. A hierarchy that is too flat therefore oscillates and one that is too deep cannot be steered in time, leaving a bounded window of depth between an unstable flat phase and a frozen inertial phase. We further show that these results can be generalised by treating each layer as a real-space renormalisation step, classifying aggregation rules by how they transmit bias. This establishes a connection between these dynamic results to attention in Transformers, where a residual update is diffusion on the token graph and depth plays the role of scale. Finally we show these phase boundaries are observable in finite sampling, and propose measurements which may characterise the proposed phases in real adaptive systems.

papers.title: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) capture global low-frequency structure during the early stage of training and then refine localized high-frequency details, afterwards. However, standard optimizers are agnostic to the coarse-to-fine learning behavior of INRs. Such optimizers accumulate a gradient matrix in momentum buffer and retain components misaligned with the dominant low-frequency directions in the early stage. We propose a progressively growing rank scheduler and a rank-aware learning-rate scheduler for enhancing a subspace-based momentum optimization, where a momentum matrix is updated within a low-rank subspace. The rank schedule expands the subspace during training, and the scheduler holds the peak learning rate through rank growth so that the added subspace contributes to fine-detail recovery. Experiments on image fitting, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and neural radiance field optimization show that the proposed method improves convergence and peak reconstruction quality over competitive optimizers. The largest gains appear in the high-frequency refinement stage, mirroring the coarse-to-fine progression that the rank schedule targets. A significant study on hyperparameter optimization (HPO) on NeRF further confirms that these gains persist under matched search budgets.

papers.title: Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
papers.abstract: We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. For three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. Below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. At and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. We also quantify the cost of control. The minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted Fourier norm of its periodised defect. For a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of Fourier degree at most $N$ grows linearly in $N$, i.e. Liouville ratios produce superpolynomial growth along subsequences. We derive constructive approximation estimates and sharp worst-case cost--accuracy rates on Sobolev classes of defects. For an arbitrary number of sources, the long-time classification and the quantitative estimates are governed by simultaneous Diophantine approximation of the source positions.

papers.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
papers.abstract: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points. We prove that the sign of each passive eigenvalue equals the sign of the extinct species' density in the enlarged community, that every partial community containing $X_1$ is a saddle with one unstable direction for each extinct consumer, and that the coexistence state is the only stable fixed point. A WKB treatment of the master equation gives a $2N$-dimensional Hamiltonian whose fluctuational fixed points are obtained in closed form. The resulting extinction network has $3^{N-1}$ fluctuation-driven transitions, and its coarse-grained dynamics yield an exact recursion for every mean extinction time. We analyse the three-species omnivory module in full, including a minimal set of existence conditions, global stability of coexistence, numerical instanton actions for all nine transitions and the most probable extinction route, which we confirm with stochastic simulations. Finally, we show how deleting a single trophic link reshapes the extinction network.

papers.title: Equilibrium finiteness and Saari's conjecture for the planar circular restricted N-body problem
papers.abstract: We establish two results for planar Newtonian centers in uniform rotation. First, the associated quadratic-plus-Newtonian amended potential has finitely many equilibria for every finite configuration of at least two distinct centers with positive masses. Second, every collision-free planar test-particle motion with constant amended potential, equivalently constant rotating-frame speed, is stationary in the rotating frame. When the centers are primary bodies in a circular relative equilibrium, this proves the amended-potential form of Saari's conjecture for the restricted \(N\)-body problem.

papers.title: Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning for Backdoor Removal
papers.abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a severe threat to modern NLP models by embedding hidden triggers that induce malicious behavior at inference time. Recent unlearning methods such as gradient ascent (GA) attempt to remove backdoors by maximizing the loss on poisoned samples; however, these methods can suffer from a critical limitation: they may shift the trigger's influence to other classes rather than eliminating it. In this work, we propose Trigger-Invariant Contrastive Unlearning (TICU), a framework for mitigating textual backdoor behavior by enforcing prediction and representation invariance to trigger insertion. TICU constructs clean and trigger-inserted counterfactual pairs, then fine-tunes the model so that both inputs produce consistent output distributions and aligned hidden representations. To preserve clean-task performance, TICU also retains the supervised classification loss on clean data and constrains parameter drift from the original model. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets, model architectures, and attack settings show that TICU improves triggered accuracy and reduces trigger-induced prediction shifts compared with existing baselines, while maintaining competitive label-flipping performance and limiting clean-task degradation.

papers.title: Reflection subgroups and the Lookup Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Lookup Conjecture of Boe-Graham proposes a Bruhat graph criterion for rational smoothness of Schubert varieties in the flag variety $\mathcal{G}/\mathcal{B}$ of a complex reductive group. Its extension to Kac-Moody groups of affine type $\widetilde{A}_n$ was considered by Graham-Li. We prove the original conjecture as well as its extension to $\widetilde{A}_n$. Our method could be applied more generally to any Kac-Moody group after checking the rank-three reflection subgroups of its Weyl group. We also prove a parabolic version of the Lookup Conjecture for the type $A$ affine Grassmannian, where a stronger Bruhat graph degree monotonicity property in fact holds, and discuss the implication via the geometric Satake correspondence for weight multiplicities.

papers.title: Spectral bounds of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems: monotonicity, domain limits, and applications
papers.abstract: We study the spectral bound of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems on bounded domains. The spectral bound is continuous under uniform coefficient and suitable nested domain perturbations, and strictly monotone with respect to the coefficients and the domain if either corresponding operator admits a principal eigenvalue. Further results include small-domain limits, large-domain limits for even convolution kernels under suitable coefficient assumptions, and criteria for a unique critical domain size. Applications yield a unique extinction-persistence threshold in the interval length for a heterogeneous epidemic model and a sharp spreading-vanishing threshold for a scalar free-boundary problem. These thresholds remain valid when the spectral bound vanishes on an interval, with the critical habitat length given by its right endpoint.

papers.title: PACL: Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting framework for bound-preserving compact single-step DG methods for hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: We develop a Patch-based Admissibility and Conservative Limiting (PACL) framework for compact single-step discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of hyperbolic conservation laws. The key idea is to establish admissibility of weighted averages over overlapping cell patches after a complete high-order time step. Continuous patch weights cancel interior numerical flux contributions, yielding admissibility estimates for weighted patch averages under suitable time-step conditions. A conservative patch correction uses these averages as reference states to obtain admissible physical cell averages, and a subsequent cellwise scaling enforces whole-cell or nodal admissibility in the original DG space. The framework requires neither a strong-stability-preserving decomposition nor auxiliary first-order discretizations, and all limiting is performed at the end of each time step. For scalar conservation laws, we prove a patchwise weak maximum principle for compact Runge--Kutta DG (cRKDG), ADER-DG with converged or fixed-Picard predictors, and Lax--Wendroff DG. We also prove that, under the stated local mesh and scaling assumptions, a single application of the scalar limiter preserves approximation order at active bounds, including flat extrema. For the compressible Euler equations, we establish patch admissibility for cRKDG and fixed-Picard ADER-DG under time-step conditions that maintain positive predictor density while allowing nonpositive predictor pressure. The analysis covers both exact spatial integration and compatible quadrature. Numerical experiments demonstrate high-order accuracy and bound preservation, including problems with near-vacuum states and strong shocks.

papers.title: Reflections in graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce and study an operation on graphs, called edge reflection, modeled on the effect of a reflection on the inversion graph of a permutation. The edge reflection length of a graph counts the fewest edge reflections needed to reduce it to the edgeless graph. Emptying a graph one edge at a time, or one vertex at a time, gives two upper bounds on this length, and each holds with equality precisely when the graph is a forest. For the edge bound we say more: the cyclomatic number of the graph bounds, above and below, the difference between the graph's size and its edge reflection length. Returning to permutations, we show that the edge reflection length of an inversion graph is at most the reflection length of any permutation realizing it, with equality whenever each connected component of the inversion graph has cyclomatic number at most one.

papers.title: Symmetry-Aware Residual Learning of Few-Body Molecular Wave Functions
papers.abstract: Ultracold polar molecules are a highly controllable platform for engineering quantum matter, but modeling their few-body properties remains computationally challenging. Their anisotropic long-range interactions and rich internal structure lead to high-dimensional eigenvalue problems for which conventional grid-based solvers are largely restricted to two-molecule systems. To address this limitation, we introduce a physics-informed neural variational method that exploits known physical structure of the molecular wave function. Our key idea is to factor the wave function into analytic and neural components. The analytic component encodes rotational symmetry and asymptotic decay, while the neural residual learns the remaining intermediate-range behavior. This decomposition reduces the effective dimensionality of the problem without relying on ad hoc approximations or problem-specific discretization grids. We benchmark our method against high-accuracy two-molecule solvers and recover both ground and excited bound states with mean relative errors below 0.01%. We further demonstrate the method's applicability to three-body systems by computing field-linked trimer ground-state energies in percent-level agreement with an independent grid-based calculation. This provides a systematic route to larger molecular systems and opens opportunities to study correlations and dynamics in interacting quantum matter.

papers.title: DoseSteer: Steering diffusion-based dose prediction models towards clinical targets via Dual-Response Guidance
papers.abstract: AI dose-prediction models generate patient-specific 3D dose distributions from patient anatomy. Yet these predictions can still miss structure-level clinical dose targets. Once deployed, most existing predictors offer no direct mechanism to correct such deviations, deferring target enforcement to downstream plan optimization. We introduce DoseSteer, an inference-time framework that steers frozen diffusion-based dose prediction models towards specified clinical targets without retraining. To meet clinical targets while preserving overall dose prediction quality, we propose Dual-Response Guidance (DRG), a structure-centric algorithm that probes the model's responses to perturbations in each structure's noisy dose and context and jointly solves for per-structure steering strengths. Across five dataset-model configurations spanning three diffusion architectures and three datasets, DRG outperforms 12 training-free baselines under identical reference-derived target proxies, removing at least 97% of the target error, reducing the official dose error by 7.8% on average, and improving dose fidelity outside the steered structures. DoseSteer reconciles learned anatomical dose priors with explicit structure-level targets at test time, establishing a principled, training-free mechanism to refine AI dose predictions prior to plan optimization. Code is available at https://github.com/csp2002/DoseSteer.

papers.title: Co-amenability and local reflexivity of $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A\subset B$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras. We prove that local reflexivity passes from $A$ to $B$ if the inclusion $A^{**}\subset B^{**}$ is co-amenable. It follows that local reflexivity is preserved by minimal tensor products with exact $C^*$-algebras, by inductive limits over directed sets, and by reduced crossed products by discrete amenable groups. We also prove that reduced free products with respect to states with faithful GNS representations preserve local reflexivity and that every locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra embeds into a simple locally reflexive $C^*$-algebra. These results answer Questions~(b), (c), (d), (f) and~(h) in Kirchberg's 2011 list.

papers.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
papers.abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. Even with arms attached, DexEngine tracks objects more accurately than prior floating-hand methods and runs over 10x faster than RL-based ones. Policies trained on our data far outperform those trained on the same clips without physics correction or with the arms attached after a floating-hand correction, showing that fine-tuning data need physics correction. Mid-training on our data further improves them at equal fine-tuning budget, in simulation and on a real robot.

papers.title: LLMVC: Large Language Model-Guided Generative Video Compression
papers.abstract: Recent generative video methods achieve strong perceptual compression by encoding videos into compact latent representations and reconstructing them with powerful generative decoders. However, visual encoders must compress both high-level semantics and dense visual details into a unified latent space, which complicates entropy coding and decoding and may cause semantic drift under aggressive compression. In this work, we propose Large Language Model-Guided Video Compression (LLMVC), which leverages the summarization capability of frozen video large language models (Video-LLMs) to generate compact semantic tokens aligned with temporal latent slices for guiding video compression. Specifically, Hybrid Bidirectional Bimodal Attention (HBBA) enables bidirectional interactions between visual and semantic features during encoding and decoding. Semantic-Conditioned Cross-Attention (SCCA) incorporates semantic features into probability modeling during entropy coding. These semantic features provide high-level guidance throughout the pipeline, improving representation quality and encouraging semantic consistency through a transmitted text side channel. Experiments on UVG, MCL-JCV, and HEVC show that LLMVC consistently improves compression performance over traditional and recent neural video compression methods in terms of LPIPS and DISTS, while also achieving better fidelity than recent perceptual codecs.

papers.title: Evaluating Strategies for Multimodal Bidirectional Interactions between Pedestrians and AVs
papers.abstract: Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) share spaces with Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs) in encounters where driver cues are absent. This can leave people uncertain whether the vehicle has noticed them and understood their request. Existing research has studied how AVs communicate with pedestrians through external human-machine interfaces. This work investigates bidirectional multimodal VRU-AV interactions combining Augmented Reality (AR), speech, and gestures. The study follows four stages: literature synthesis of interactions, a survey with 124 participants, interaction loop implementation, and feasibility evaluation. Participants preferred AR cues that made vehicle motion or warnings explicit, high-level voice commands, and conventional gestures. Prototype measurements revealed a trade-off between faster local processing and more accurate infrastructure-assisted processing. The demonstration shows bidirectional interaction using AR wearables and vehicular communications, while leaving decision-making to the AV. Together, the results support treating AV-VRU interaction as a closed loop of intent expression, recognition, vehicle decision, and feedback.

papers.title: Unsupervised and explainable authorization of change point in multivariate industrial data for trustworthy system and process monitoring
papers.abstract: The paper introduces a Change point Hypothesis Assessment for Significance in Multivariate data (CHASM) - a novel non-parametric approach for evaluating the significance of change points detected in multivariate data, especially relevant for a trustworthy autonomous industrial system. The method is highly scalable, doesn't require data labeling, and allows for customizable evaluation criteria, such as inter-component relationships. Its non-parametric nature broadens applicability to non-Gaussian distributed data. CHASM incorporates robust auxiliary statistics that maintain reliability even in the presence of outliers, enabling accurate assessment of change point significance for complex data. Beyond statistical significance testing, CHASM also facilitates root-cause analysis of detected changes. It offers a solution expected by practitioners for validating change points identified by segmentation-based algorithms, particularly those lacking rigorous statistical foundations. To support situation aware decision making, a {trustworthy factor} is introduced and its performance demonstrated for simulated and real-world data recorded in machine monitoring system. Using MAPE, it was evidenced that the two-stage procedure - identification of the change point and authorization of the change point - significantly outperforms (23-fold in the reported experiment) the one-stage scheme. All these are essential in real-world applications, where overfitting and false alarms can lead to loss of trust in technical solutions.

papers.title: Solving the capacitated vehicle routing problem with polygonal neighborhoods using a metaheuristic enhanced with block coordinate descent
papers.abstract: We study a capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP) in which customers are represented by planar regions, called customer neighborhoods, rather than fixed points. Visiting a customer consists of selecting a point within its neighborhood. Therefore, besides determining the sequence of customers visited by each vehicle, one must also determine the corresponding visit points. To better reflect practical applications, customer neighborhoods are allowed to be simple polygons, either convex or non-convex, and distances are measured using the Euclidean norm. Applications include aerial reconnaissance, wireless sensor data collection and inspection, and two-stage delivery systems. We propose a general variable neighborhood search framework in which each neighbor is represented by a collection of routes. Constructing a route involves two stages, defining a customer sequence and then determining the associated visit points. The latter task is solved by a block coordinate descent (BCD) procedure, the central methodological contribution of this work, which computes high-quality visit points at a cost low enough to be used repeatedly inside the search. In extensive experiments on newly generated and adapted benchmark instances, within the time limits considered, the proposed framework matches all solutions proven optimal by CPLEX and matches or improves the best solutions found by CPLEX in the remaining instances. For the instances adapted from the CVRP literature, it also improves, in every instance, a CVRP-based upper bound given by the solution of the original CVRP instance reported in the literature, which is feasible for the problem with neighborhoods.

papers.title: How LLM Agents Reshape Financial Knowledge Graphs: A Survey
papers.abstract: Financial knowledge graphs (KGs) link information across sources to support risk assessment, investment research, asset recommendations, and forecasting. Large language models (LLMs) help build these graphs by extracting relationships from text and matching entities across records. Yet a workflow may still prescribe which sources to consult and which checks to run. If the chosen sources lack relevant evidence, even accurate extraction can leave a financial question unanswered. LLM agents can adapt the workflow as evidence emerges. They use the graph and earlier findings to decide where to look next, which claims to verify, and whether to update a record for later use. This is the first survey devoted to how LLM agents reshape the construction, maintenance, and use of financial KGs. Our taxonomy covers Knowledge Graph Construction, Temporal Evolution, Verification, Reconciliation, and Admission, Adaptive Acquisition, and Knowledge Graph Usage. We examine how studies evaluate graph quality, agents' use of evidence, financial task outcomes, and reliability over time. These evaluations show that agents can recover evidence missed in an initial search and revise records as new information arrives. Three questions remain unresolved. How can an agent tell whether it has enough evidence for a financial decision? After a record is corrected, how can the agent identify which earlier conclusions need to change? Which relationships and rules can it reuse in a new graph or domain?

papers.title: Sharp sensitivity bounds and maximin policy learning under violations of principal ignorability
papers.abstract: Identification of assignment effects among compliers often relies on the untestable assumption of principal ignorability. Sensitivity analyses based only on outcome means and ranges can admit complier distributions incompatible with the observed data. We develop a distributional sensitivity model preserving the full observed outcome distributions and identified complier proportions. The challenge is to recover latent complier distributions within observed mixtures while ensuring compatibility across assignment arms. We characterize exactly which pairs arise from a single compatible full-data law, obtaining sharp bounds on effects and policy values. This characterization shows how complier proportions constrain departures from principal ignorability and why informative bounds remain without a finite sensitivity restriction. Accounting for principal scores in both population weights and sensitivity limits, we establish conditions for doubly robust consistency, semiparametric efficiency, and conservative bounds under quantile misspecification. Double robustness requires consistent principal score estimation. We also develop maximin decision-tree policies with value consistency and inference guarantees. Numerical studies demonstrate gains from retaining distributional information, and an Oregon Health Insurance Experiment application examines implications for complier effects and assignment policies.

papers.title: DFLAT: Model-based Diffusion on Differentially Flat Spaces for Long-Horizon Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Long-horizon diffusion-based planning for kinodynamically constrained systems requires both scalability and feasibility, yet existing diffusion planners typically sacrifice one for the other. We present DFLAT, a diffusion-based planning algorithm that operates directly on a differentially flat trajectory representation. Instead of diffusing over time-discretized controls, DFLAT denoises a compact set of Hermite curve parameters in the flat-output space, consisting of intermediate waypoints together with the endpoint tangents of each segment. Every denoised sample maps to a dynamically consistent trajectory, so feasibility holds by construction rather than being restored afterward. Experiments on challenging tractor-trailer planning benchmarks show that DFLAT matches or exceeds the success rates of existing baselines at consistently lower planning times, particularly on long-horizon problems requiring multiple forward-reverse maneuvers. In cases where kinodynamic RRT requires over 100 seconds, DFLAT plans in subsecond time, enabling practical deployment.

papers.title: Geometry-Time Graph Attention for 3-D TOA Localization in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
papers.abstract: In underwater acoustic sensor networks, depth-dependent variations in sound speed refract acoustic rays, complicating the estimation of target positions from travel-time measurements. Propagation-model-based methods rely on an assumed or estimated sound speed profile (SSP), and a mismatch between that profile and the current environment can bias position estimates. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an underwater graph attention network (UGAN) that fuses synchronized time-of-arrival (TOA) observations from multiple stations with reference-station coordinates to estimate three-dimensional target positions without requiring the current sound speed profile at inference. UGAN constructs one graph per target for batch inference. Its geometry--time attention mechanism combines interstation geometry with ordered pairs of TOA observations to compute attention weights in all three graph layers and enrich the messages in the last two layers. A shared nonlinear encoder supplies individual TOA features directly to every layer. In ray-tracing simulations with a fixed five-station deployment and two SSPs held out from training and validation, UGAN achieves mean localization root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.307, 0.577, and 0.989~m at three increasing TOA noise levels, representing reductions of 52.0\%, 31.0\%, and 22.8\% relative to the evaluated GATv2 baseline, respectively. At the intermediate noise level, incorporating station-pair relations into the messages reduces the mean localization RMSE by 9.4\% with relation-based attention scoring enabled. For 4,000 target observations, UGAN takes a median of 58.14~ms on the same GPU, 7.0\% less time than GATv2.

papers.title: SEEL: Towards End-to-End 3D Sign Generation with Language Models
papers.abstract: 3D sign language generation aims to produce signing motion from written text. Motivated by the linguistic nature of sign language, recent methods combine a motion tokenizer with a language model to predict motion tokens from text. However, both components are optimized through a two-stage pipeline with mismatched objectives: the tokenizer minimizes reconstruction error in isolation, while the generator learns from rigid one-hot reference tokens. A straightforward end-to-end extension bridges discrete token selection with straight-through estimators (STE), suffering from biased gradients and codebook collapse. To address these limitations, we propose SEEL, an end-to-end framework that aligns tokenization and generation with motion quality through two complementary mechanisms. First, to overcome rigid one-hot supervision, reconstruction-aware generation decodes candidate tokens in context and converts their 3D motion errors into soft targets, guiding the generator with physical motion quality. Second, to propagate generation feedback without STE, generation-aware tokenization passes continuous codebook expectations through the frozen generator, routing generated-motion gradients to the tokenizer to prevent codebook collapse. Combining both mechanisms enables the tokenizer and generator to co-evolve, achieving state-of-the-art performance on CSL-Daily, How2Sign, and Phoenix-2014T. Code and models will be released to facilitate future research.

papers.title: Amortizing Exact Orthogonality: Drift-Triggered Restoration for Orthogonal Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Orthogonal finetuning (OFT) adapts a pretrained weight by an orthogonal transform and preserves its singular values and row angles, but existing methods construct an exact or approximate orthogonal transform at every optimization step. We measure how far a transform $A$ is from orthogonal by its orthogonality defect $\|A^\top A-I\|_2$. For OFTv2, which truncates a Cayley-Neumann series, we show that the truncation order does not determine the defect. At its default order, block defects in checkpoints from the reference implementation span five orders of magnitude. We propose Restarted Tangent Orthogonal Finetuning (RTOFT), which uses the first-order update $W(I+S)$ of a weight $W$ with a skew-symmetric $S$ and restores exact orthogonality by a polar decomposition only when the drift $\|S\|_2$ reaches a tolerance $τ$. The defect of $I+S$ is exactly $\|S\|_2^2$. Therefore, reading the drift after every update and restoring before the next forward pass guarantees a defect of at most $τ^2$ in every forward pass, independently of the loss, data, model, and optimizer. A final restoration makes the returned transform exactly orthogonal. On GLUE, RTOFT reduces the training time of block-diagonal, subspace, and butterfly parameterizations from $1.10$-$1.58\times$ to $0.97$-$1.13\times$ that of LoRA, and its block-diagonal version exceeds LoRA by $1.98\pm0.39$ points on the six-task average over five seeds. At $τ=0.10$, the largest drift read during training stays between $0.10$ and $0.12$ across DeBERTaV3, Qwen, and diffusion models, whereas it ranges from $0.17$ to $1.65$ when restoring once per epoch. In all seven settings of our ablation, the tangent update is worse without restoration than with it, and restoring after every step yields no measurable accuracy gain over restoring at the tolerance and costs $4.5$-$27.5\%$ more per step.

papers.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below $10^{-10}$ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm $\times$ 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.

papers.title: VivaWorld: Long-Horizon Video World Model With Compositional 3D Priors
papers.abstract: Long-horizon video generation is key to interactive world modeling, physical intelligence, and spatial reasoning, yet maintaining geometric consistency and accurate camera control remains challenging without 3D grounding. We introduce \textbf{VivaWorld}, a framework for generating geometry- and view-consistent long videos from an image. We first construct a compositional hybrid 3D representation that combines reconstructed point clouds, which preserve observed scene geometry and appearance, with generated textured meshes, which provide complete object geometry across $360^\circ$ novel views. We also introduce a connected-region filter removing inconsistent floating components for robust cross-view reconstruction and propose a hybrid camera embedding that combines global and object-anchored Plücker rays to capture both scene-level camera motion and camera-object relationships, and inject it together with the visual guidance into a video generation model via a control adapter. Extensive experiments show VivaWorld achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and camera control, while supporting controllable novel-view synthesis, long-horizon scene exploration, and physical AI. Project page is available at: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/sil/projects/vivaworld/

papers.title: Improved Sample Complexity of Robust Reinforcement Learning with KL Uncertainty Sets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study distributionally robust reinforcement learning with Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence-defined uncertainty sets. The goal is to find a policy that maximizes the robust value function, defined as the worst-case value over all transition kernels in the uncertainty set. Assuming access to a generative model, we aim to understand the sample complexity of finding an $ε$-optimal robust policy. The best-known sample complexity results in the literature show a non-trivial gap of $\mathcal{O}\{\max\{p_\wedge^{-1}(1-γ)^{-1},(1-γ)^{-2}\}\}$ between the upper and lower bounds, where $p_\wedge$ denotes the minimum positive transition probability of the nominal transition kernel, and $γ$ is the discount factor. More importantly, existing results on the lower bound only cover a limited range of the uncertainty level. In this paper, we develop tighter and complete upper and lower bounds for robust RL with KL-defined uncertainty sets. Our upper bound is the tightest among all existing studies, and it improves upon the best-known bound by at least the order of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{p_\wedge^{-1},(1-γ)^{-1}\})$ for uncertainty level $δ\in(0,1)$. Furthermore, our lower bound holds for any uncertainty level. Our upper and lower bounds (nearly) match in various regimes, providing improved results for this problem.

papers.title: Optimization of a Hybrid Solar-Biogas-Battery Energy Storage Microgrid: A Case Study
papers.abstract: Low-income regions like eastern Uganda often lack reliable grid power. This paper presents the techno-economic optimization of the Soroti Integrated Renewable Energy Microgrid (SIREM), a hybrid renewable system for grid-access expansion where Soroti District household grid access stands at 16.7\%. The microgrid integrates concentrating solar power (CSP) with thermal storage, biogas combined cycle generation, and lithium iron phosphate battery storage. Using Xendee optimization software with six years of NASA POWER data, the optimal configuration comprises a 37 MW CSP field, 70 MWh molten-salt storage, a 5 MW CSP turbine, a 6 MW biogas CCGT, and a 10 MWh battery system. The design delivers 61.3 GWh annually with a 42.91% IRR, 2-year payback, and levelized cost of electricity of 0.1991 USD/kWh generation (0.3752 USD/kWh load-served), achieving 32.2% total savings versus grid-only supply while exporting 28.8 GWh annually, demonstrating the viability of hybrid renewable microgrids for grid expansion in sub-Saharan Africa.

papers.title: Aligned Machine: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Embedding Similarity via Human Comparative Judgements
papers.abstract: Embedding models increasingly inform how people search, recommend, and retrieve information, yet we lack credible ways to test whether these similarity judgments reflect how humans understand meaning. Existing benchmarks typically rely on static, expert-labeled pairs with coarse Likert-style annotations, limiting scalability and making it difficult to obtain consistent, high-confidence annotations. We introduce Aligned Machine, an interactive, public-facing platform that transforms broad participation into a continuously growing Human-Aligned Similarity Benchmark (HASB) for evaluating semantic alignment in embedding-based systems. Participants complete a cognitively-natural, forced-choice task, comparing two pairs of items (text or images) and selecting which pair is more similar. This comparative design is accessible to non-experts, yields clean preference data, and supports robust aggregation. We report results from an initial deployment with 115 participants contributing 2,875 total labeled pairs and 872 unique pairs. Using HASB, we evaluated 12 widely used embedding models and found only partial alignment between embedding similarity and human judgments. Text-only models consistently achieve higher overall agreement than multimodal models, while multimodal performance varies systematically by task type: alignment is strongest for image-image comparisons, weaker for image-text comparisons, and lowest for text-text comparisons. Aligned Machine is designed to evolve over time as participation grows, supporting longitudinal analysis, domain-specific studies, bias detection, and measurement of concept drift across model versions. By combining accessible public participation with rigorous comparative evaluation, HASB provides a scalable and accountable framework for auditing semantic alignment in embedding models.

papers.title: Small Leaks Sink Great Ships: Automated Analysis of Protocols That Tolerate Low-Entropy Keys
papers.abstract: Modern cryptographic protocols such as WPA2-PSK, Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), and Bluetooth Classic (BC) tolerate low-entropy keys for user-friendliness, backward compatibility, or resource-constrained deployment, yet existing symbolic protocol verifiers rely on the perfect-encryption assumption and therefore cannot reason about brute-force attackers. Prior work addresses this gap only through protocol-specific, manually encoded reveal rules, which neither generalize across protocols nor systematically explore compound-key decomposition. We introduce the first protocol-agnostic, automated symbolic methodology for low-entropy keys, built on three abstractions: the message-derivation fact MDerive, which captures brute-force prerequisites independently of concrete function symbols; a three-tier breaking-oracle design (value-breaking, relationship-breaking, message-derivation) that composes with the standard Dolev-Yao attacker; and a graded bit-level attacker model that bounds the key length an attacker is allowed to exhaust. We realize the methodology as EntropyVerif, a syntax-sugar extension of Tamarin that requires no kernel modification. Using EntropyVerif we automatically rediscover the PMKID, KNOB, and Method Confusion attacks, and uncover a new attack on BC which we call the Unilateral Multi-Downgrade (UMD) attack: by repeatedly downgrading one side of a BC session and recombining the recovered key fragments, an attacker reduces session-key recovery against devices using the maximum 128-bit key from $2^{128}$ to $n \cdot 2^{128/n}$, bottoming out at $2^{12}$ for $n=16$---a factor of $2^{116}$ reduction that has been responsibly disclosed to the Bluetooth SIG. Across three real-world protocols and six BC device configurations, our results show that entropy-aware symbolic analysis is both feasible and necessary.

papers.title: k-Nearest Neighbors estimation of the drift of an ergodic diffusion process under Osgood regularity
papers.abstract: The k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) algorithm is a widely used machine learning method with well-established theoretical guarantees for consistent estimation in multivariate settings and functional time series analysis. In the context of nonparametric estimation of the coefficients of ergodic diffusion processes, however, its use has so far been mainly illustrated through numerical experiments. The main contribution of this paper is to establish theoretical consistency results for drift kNN estimators over both compact and non-compact intervals, under relatively weak regularity conditions on the coefficients of the underlying ergodic diffusion process. The theoretical results are completed with numerical illustrations.

papers.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.

papers.title: Transport of High Energy Protons from CME-Shock to the Sun and its Connection to Extended Gamma-rays Observed by FERMI
papers.abstract: This work is motivated by the Large Area Telescope (LAT) observations of long-duration gamma rays from flares associated often with fast Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs), several of which originate behind the limb (BTL) of the Sun. Our aim is to test the feasibility of the scenario whereby the gamma-rays are produced by CME-shock accelerated particles escaping from downstream to the Sun by investigating the transport of protons in this process for the flare of 2014 September 1. We use results from the global MHD modeling by the Alfvén Wave Solar Model (AWSoM) to obtain the characteristics of downstream plasma, such as magnetic field geometry, Alfvén speed, and energy density of turbulence. This allows us to evaluate the variations of the proton scattering mean free path with energy and distance from the CME-shock. Using an approximate analytic relation between the relevant time scales of the transport, we determine the energy dependence of the residence time at (or escape time from) different distances above the photosphere, and determine the evolution of the proton spectrum from the acceleration site to the photosphere. These results can be used to obtain the spectrum of the observed gamma-rays. Inversely, because of insignificant energy loss or gain during transport, this is a reversible process and the spectrum of protons at the photosphere, obtained from the observed gamma-rays, can be ``de-evolved" back to the CME using the same algorithm. Comparison of these spectra with the in situ observations of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) could then shed light on their transport from the CME to the Earth.

papers.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
papers.abstract: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

papers.title: Refinements to precision-information imputation in meta-analysis of survival rates: Boundary correction and cross-study borrowing
papers.abstract: Meta-analyses of survival rates require precision information, such as standard errors (SEs), which is often unreported. We previously proposed imputing missing SEs from reported survival rates, sample sizes, and risk-set sizes. The original method has two limitations. First, it replaces Kaplan--Meier estimates of 1 with 0.99 regardless of sample size. Second, when the risk-set size is unavailable, it uses the total event count as a fallback. The count is often unreported, and the fallback can also substantially overestimate SEs. We propose a sample-size-dependent boundary correction based on a pseudo-event and a method that borrows time-specific event information from studies with available risk-set sizes. In simulations, the boundary correction was more stable than fixed replacement, and borrowing reduced study-level SE imputation bias. Borrowing generally improved precision by retaining studies with missing SEs that lacked both risk-set sizes and event counts.

papers.title: Cohomology growth for pseudoeffective line bundles on compact Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a pseudoeffective line bundle with a singular metric $h$ satisfying $Θ_h(L)\geq0$ on a compact Kähler manifold $X$ of dimension $n$. Let $\mathcal{I}(h^k)$ denote the multiplier ideal sheaf of $h^k$. For every holomorphic vector bundle $E$ and $0\le q\le n$, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim}_{\mathbb{C}}H^q\!\left(X,E\otimes L^k\otimes\mathcal{I}(h^k)\right)=O(k^{n-q}),$$ which gives an affirmative answer to Matsumura's growth problem. As an application, we resolve the cohomology growth problem for nef line bundles raised by Demailly.

papers.title: Differential coupling drives Turing pattern formation in neural fields: a mechanism for Parkinson's disease and deep brain stimulation
papers.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an effective treatment for the motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Abnormal beta-band synchronization in the basal ganglia and thalamocortical circuit is a hallmark of PD, but a theoretical framework linking network synchronization to spatial pattern formation is lacking. Here we show that a two-layer neural field model with differential interlayer coupling undergoes a Turing instability, spontaneously generating a diverse repertoire of spatially ordered patterns, including stripes, spots, rings, and spiral waves. The model yields the critical conditions and wavelengths for this instability, quantitatively predicting the observed pattern morphologies. Crucially, the interlayer difference, a natural measure of synchrony, exhibits strongly regime dependent dynamics. These findings establish a dynamical framework linking spatial pattern formation to pathological beta-band synchronization, providing a theoretical mechanism for DBS modulation of network states and a mathematical basis for optimizing stimulation parameters.

papers.title: Retirement Planning with Borrowing Constraints and Income Support
papers.abstract: We study how pension income, its pledgeability, and government support that supplements effective consumption shape an irreversible retirement decision. In a continuous-time life-cycle model, a worker chooses consumption, risky investment, and the timing of retirement, subject to a tighter borrowing limit after retirement. When retirement reduces the utility value of a given level of effective consumption, immediate retirement can be optimal on a bounded wealth interval: a worker below the interval retires when wealth rises to its lower boundary, while a worker above it retires when wealth falls to its upper boundary. Two scalar boundary equations characterize these distinct entry points. Risky investment drops discretely upon retirement at either interior boundary, even when it rises with wealth along the low-wealth working branch. In our two-boundary baseline, greater income support lowers the lower retirement threshold and raises the upper one, whereas greater pension pledgeability shifts both thresholds downward. Finally, because the residuals of the boundary equations represent weighted tail integrals of the instantaneous gain from postponing retirement, we completely characterize the optimal retirement region across all levels of post-retirement quality of life.

papers.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
papers.abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and étale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.

papers.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. However, such recovery may preserve task functionality while silently discarding the security protections required by the original workflow. In this paper, we investigate workflow security downgrade, a failure-induced security threat in which agents execute sensitive operations without satisfying their original protection requirements. Unlike prompt injection, this threat exploits autonomous recovery decisions triggered by execution failures, without modifying instructions or tool definitions. We systematically evaluate this behavior through fault injection in an executable MCP/Skill environment spanning seven LLMs, twelve task templates, and three security-sensitive domains. To address this threat, we propose ARGUS, an obligation-preserving recovery framework that combines resource-bound security evidence, isolated recovery-plan validation, and execution-time enforcement. In a separate 864-run evaluation, ARGUS prevents all observed protection-loss events under enforcement, while recovery assistance yields model-dependent improvements in protected task completion over blocking alone. Our findings demonstrate that secure agent recovery requires preserving security obligations across workflow changes, rather than merely restoring task functionality.

papers.title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.

papers.title: A Robust Approach for Regression Analysis of Panel Count Data with Time-varying Covariates
papers.abstract: The validity of statistical inference for panel count data with time-varying covariates depends on the correct specification of within-subject correlation structures; misspecification often leads to questionable inference. To alleviate, robust inference has been proposed for mean models, which implicitly assume monotone mean functions. When covariate values fluctuate with time, however, the assumed monotonicity becomes unrealistic. In this research, we propose a robust inference based on rate models that are free of such constraints. Since the asymptotic variance has no closed form under the rate model, we further develop computationally efficient robust variance estimators using the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm, thus sidestepping the need for computationally intensive numerical methods, which could undermine the robustness. Rigorous theoretical development is provided in support of parameter estimation and inference. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method. We present a real clinical application to illustrate the use of the proposed method.

papers.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.

papers.title: Reeb stability for singular Riemannian foliations
papers.abstract: We prove a global Reeb stability theorem for singular Riemannian foliations on compact connected manifolds using the semi-local model developed by Alexandrino et al. We show that all leaves are compact if and only if the foliation is infinitesimally closed, and there exists a compact leaf with a linear holonomy groupoid which is proper at that leaf. These conditions are also equivalent to the existence of a smooth map to a Euclidean space whose fibers are exactly the leaves. The proof combines a local criterion for strong stability with compact transverse leaves, Molino's structural theory, and polynomial descriptions of local leaf spaces. Around a closed leaf, we show that the linear holonomy groupoid realizes the original foliation precisely when the infinitesimal foliation is homogeneous. When the infinitesimal foliation is closed, properness of this groupoid yields an associated-bundle model whose compact structure group is its isotropy group. We also characterize the existence, near a compact leaf, of a Hausdorff model Lie groupoid which is proper at that leaf. As an application, we obtain stability results for maps whose connected fiber components form singular Riemannian foliations. We compare linear holonomy with Fernandes's reduced Lie algebroid holonomy and with formal outer holonomy. Finally, we prove that, for every infinitesimally closed singular Riemannian foliation, the compactly supported tangent vector fields form a locally finitely generated involutive module inducing the original leaf partition.

papers.title: Numerical Studies of Ground State Atomic Parity Violation Measurements in Cesium
papers.abstract: We report results of numerical simulations of an ongoing measurement designed to measure the electric dipole (E1) transition moment between hyperfine components of the ground state of atomic cesium. This E1 moment is non-zero solely due to nuclear weak interactions between the nucleons, leading to a nuclear anapole moment of the cesium nucleus. Through these simulations, we explore the effect on the microwave spectrum of a static transverse magnetic field, a spatial offset of the atomic beam from the axis of the radio-frequency (rf) cavity, the angular tilt of the rf cavity, and the ac Stark shift by the Raman-coupling beams used to generate the initial superposition state between ground state components. The results of these simulations help place limits on the experimental parameters, and help guide the future experimental procedures.

papers.title: Azimuthally Resolved Energy Dissipation Rates in the Impingement Zone of Equal Free Impinging Liquid Jets: A Three-Dimensional Model
papers.abstract: When two equal liquid jets collide, they form a thin sheet of liquid and lose some of their incoming kinetic energy (doi:10.1615/AtomizSpr.2025056396). Calculating the energy dissipation rate per unit mass requires estimating the volume of the region where the collision takes place. This paper develops a three-dimensional model of that region and uses it to calculate how the energy dissipation rate varies with angular position within the collision region. The model assumes that the thickness of the collision region varies linearly along each radial line from the stagnation point to its outer boundary. Combining the resulting volume with the kinetic energy lost during the collision provides equations for both the overall energy dissipation rate and the rate averaged over each narrow angular portion of the collision region (local energy dissipation rate). For equal jets with uniform inlet velocity profiles, the model predicts substantial differences in energy dissipation rate with angular position, even when the incoming jets and the resulting sheet have uniform mean velocities. The model also reproduces expected theoretical limits, including a cylindrical collision region for directly opposed jets. Preliminary micromixing results are consistent with the predicted variation, although independent validation of the assumed collision-region geometry and the location of energy dissipation is still needed.

papers.title: Failure Broadens, Success Sharpens: Continual Adaptation of Tool-Use Agents Across Diverse Tasks with Dual-Polarity Memory
papers.abstract: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios.
